title: Syncing a deleted feed can leave it active but still tombstoned

evidence.quote:
feed.is_active = False
    feed.deleted_at = now
    feed.updated_at = now

reasoning: DELETE soft-deletes a feed by setting deleted_at. Later, /sync loads all feeds, including tombstoned rows, and updates fields such as is_active without clearing deleted_at. If a client syncs the same URL after deletion with is_active=true, the row can become active while still excluded from list/changes queries that filter deleted_at == None, so the feed remains invisible despite the successful sync.
reproduction: Create a feed, DELETE /api/feeds/{id}, then POST /api/feeds/sync with the same URL and is_active=true. The sync updates the existing row but leaves deleted_at set, so GET /api/feeds still omits it.
recommendation: Define the intended conflict behavior for incoming sync data matching a tombstoned feed. If sync should restore client-present feeds, clear deleted_at when updating a deleted row. If tombstones must win, do not update is_active/title/mode on deleted rows and return a clear result.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: tests/test_feeds.py only covers empty list, create, and basic sync creation; it does not exercise DELETE followed by sync or assert tombstone restoration/conflict behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that creates a feed, deletes it, syncs the same URL as active, and asserts the row is either restored with deleted_at null and appears in GET /api/feeds, or remains tombstoned without becoming is_active=true, depending on the chosen contract.
minimumFixScope: app/api/feeds.py sync_feeds tombstoned-row handling plus a focused feed deletion/sync regression test.
